teams.synopsis: Woof, right back to the top of rankings after a dip down to 6th for a week.
teams.blurb: Woof, right back to the top of rankings after a dip down to 6th for a week. Ben went nuclear in Week 4, and then was horrible in Week 5, and now he just put up 150 in Week 6. What’s going on with this team? I mean they lead the league in points per game, they’re actually the only team to average more than 120 points per matchup, and they are tied for the best record at 4-2. So, was the poor Week 5 performance just due to Kenneth Walker III being on BYE, Lamar Jackson being injured, CeeDee Lamb putting up a dud, and Deebo Samuel getting injured during the game? I guess so, at least that’s how I’m going to look at it. The team now has a rising star in Germie Bernard, or that’s what it looks like after these past two weeks. The Week 7 matchup looks to be a tough one, as it is a prime time matchup against the 2nd ranked team in this week’s rankings, but if Ben just continues to produce like he has been (for the most part) then he should maintain this top spot heading into Week 8.

teams.synopsis: A solid win in Week 6 keeps this squad within the top five in the rankings for the 5th week in a row.
teams.blurb: A solid win in Week 6 keeps this squad within the top five in the rankings for the 5th week in a row. This is the only team to put up at least 100 points in each week this season, producing between 108 and 134 points each week. If you’re a successful team in fantasy you want to be consistent, you know you can get unlucky with some losses across a season, but if you keep producing at above league average levels then eventually you’ll overcome the unluckiness. Week 7 will be a tough one against a challenging opponent, but it should get easier after that. I really like this squad with its RBs and WRs and competent QBs, like I’ve continued to say every week, but I think the ranking should speak for itself.

teams.synopsis: Despite the win in Week 6, I have to drop Rolls With Butter down a spot in rankings due to the 97.5-point performance.
teams.blurb: Despite the win in Week 6, I have to drop Rolls With Butter down a spot in rankings due to the 97.5-point performance. Now, the team gets hit with some rough BYEs in Week 7, but they’re still projected to be somewhat competitive against what’s been a hit-or-miss squad. Anthony spent $140 on C.J. Stroud on this week’s waiver wire, a decision that was completely ripped apart in the group chat, but let’s see if it pays off against C.J. Stroud’s last manager in Week 7. Still, even if Anthony loses the Week 7 matchup, he will still have a positive record and over the worst BYE week of the season. I wish I could say more about the team but I’m tapped out. Good Luck.

teams.synopsis: Is there really any other wide receiver you’d want in fantasy aside from Jaxon Smith-Njigba?
teams.blurb: Is there really any other wide receiver you’d want in fantasy aside from Jaxon Smith-Njigba? Maybe Puka Nacua due to the Davante Adams injury and the better QB play, but it really is a toss up I think. After a tight win in Week 6 with a poor 92.6-point performance, Baylen finds himself dropping a spot in the rankings but I don’t think this team will really be dropping much more after this week. The QB “rotation” is incredible, the WR core is exactly what you want from a contender, and the TE duo is maybe the best we have ever seen from a Preach Fantasy team. Now, the RB core, or the lack there of, is concerning. But that stuff should work itself out with some trades in the coming days or weeks, or maybe even a waiver wire gem finds its way onto Station Grits and makes them an unstoppable force on track for their 2nd championship. It’s projected to be a tight high-scoring matchup in Week 7, but I think Baylen gets it done and avoids going below .500.

teams.synopsis: Yeah, man, I have no clue what to do with this team.
teams.blurb: Yeah, man, I have no clue what to do with this team. They’re middle-of-the-pack in terms of record and points per game, and they just put up sub-100 points for the second time in six weeks. I’ve gushed over this team’s depth, which ranks 2nd in the league behind Aidan’s roster, but with the loss of Terry McLaurin for the rest of 2026 that depth may take a hit. The team also lost Romeo Doubs to injury reserve, and a temporary loss of Trevor Lawrence to BYE for Week 7, but on the bright side they get Jahmyr Gibbs back from BYE, so a bounce back in Week 7 against a super weak opponent is in order. If I told you a team with a top five QB, two top fourteen RBs, two top sixteen WRs, and two top twelve TEs was a middling squad with meh success through six weeks would you be shocked? I would and I am.

teams.synopsis: This is kind of funny, not for Andrew, but after I put Ben at 1st in rankings two weeks ago he dropped to 6th in the next week, just like Andrew is now.
teams.blurb: This is kind of funny, not for Andrew, but after I put Ben at 1st in rankings two weeks ago he dropped to 6th in the next week, just like Andrew is now. Andrew still has a good team don’t get me wrong, but a 78.33-point performance and a long-term injury to Davante Adams cannot be overlooked. I still think N.Y. Routensss is firmly in position to make a playoff push, but it looks like it’ll be harder than anticipated this time last week. Andrew’s top five healthy guys, his core, combine to average about 85 points per week, which is formidable, so it will be up to the two other positions and the two special positions to pick up the slack while Davante Adams is out. Hey, maybe Marvin Harrison Jr. can break out a little bit on the Texans.

teams.synopsis: A much needed win in Week 6 gets Ryan potentially back on track.
teams.blurb: A much needed win in Week 6 gets Ryan potentially back on track. After being the luckiest manager based on schedule from 2020-2025, Ryan has taken a turn for the worse and been the most unlucky manager in the league this season, which is why I have him ranked 7th despite the poor record. Week 6 seemed like a very stress-free win, winning by about 35 points, but Week 7 appears to be almost the opposite as Ryan, the manager projected to score the most points this Week is matching up against the manager projected to score the second most points. Now that I’m saying it maybe this matchup should be the Matchup of the Week, it’s definitely a close 2nd. I think the team is really coming together, but we must keep an eye on the Aaron Jones Sr. situation.

teams.synopsis: The Gegwich Effect really put it together in Week 6, of course they did.
teams.blurb: The Gegwich Effect really put it together in Week 6, of course they did. The team is now on a three game winning streak and it looks like it’ll continue into Week 7, according to ESPN’s projections. The duo of Isaiah Likely and Malik Nabers is incredible, they remind me of Michael Wilson and Trey McBride to finish the season last year, just unreal a TE and WR on the same NFL team can put up those numbers simultaneously. The team has increased point production in each of the past three weeks, a nice trend. You must be happy if you’re Quin, right? Week 7 might the first time Quin sees his current team all play together at full strength, but a little birdie told me that the team is still looking to make some moves and get better. Let’s see if the team can extend their win streak to four games, which would tie the franchise’s record (Weeks 6-9, 2024).

teams.synopsis: He can’t keep getting away with this, can he?
teams.blurb: He can’t keep getting away with this, can he? Out of 10 teams since 2020 who have averaged less than 100 points per game, excluding Max this year of course, zero have finished with at least a .500 record and their combined record is 41-84, so what we’re seeing right now is somewhat of an anomaly that should straighten itself out if the team continues to perform the way they have. However, with the recent acquisition of Jalen Coker and the team starting to look like they could be coming together and getting healthy, I think the team could kind of flip the script and be much better from a points per game perspective in the second half of the regular season. Max currently holds the 2nd seed in the 2026 Playoff Preview, so this ranking may seem a little wrong, but once again I’m going to need to see the team actually strike fear into opponents that don’t have season-low performances. The team really looks like it’s coming together and with an easier matchup in Week 7 I think 9th could be the floor for Tee’d Up moving forward.

teams.synopsis: I feel this is a fair spot for myself.
teams.blurb: I feel this is a fair spot for myself. I want to keep this short, so simply put my team has been inconsistent, average, and I haven’t been excited often this season. Oh He Likes Cooking! has yet to cook in 2026 to the level that we expect from this team, or at least I expect from the team. Actually, 116.11 points per game is the lowest any of Ethan’s teams have had since the conception of the league. Week 7 isn’t projected to be a tough matchup based on BYEs and ESPN’s projections, but I feel the same was said going into Week 7 so let’s see what happens.

teams.synopsis: Like Carmine, Cole is having an outlier type of season and not in a good way.
teams.blurb: Like Carmine, Cole is having an outlier type of season and not in a good way. The team is averaging 107.7 points per game this season, the lowest mark since their 4-10 2022 season. They averaged between 119.5 and 129.6 points per game between 2023 and 2025, so yeah definitely an odd sight to see this franchise struggle. It also doesn’t look like it will get any better in Week 7 against what’s projected to be a real tough matchup, and if you look at the rest of season strength of schedule the team ranks first with the hardest schedule the rest of the way. It’s not looking good. On the bright side, Stefon Diggs looks like he’ll take on a bigger role since Terry McLaurin is out for the rest of the season and Jayden Daniels looks to be as good as ever. Also, Puka Nacua may genuinely go nuclear and average over 30 points while Davante Adams is out with injury. It might just be a case of “it has to get worse to get better” for Cole and his team.

What is going on? Is it the injuries or has this team simply been underwhelming? After starting the season 3-1 and being ranked within the top 10 for five of first six weeks, Carmine has fallen down to 12th with another sub-90-point performance in Week 6. The team is now one of only two within the league to average less than 100 points per matchup, and to put that into perspective for how much of an outlier this season has been for the franchise Carmine has never averaged less than 109.6 points across a full season since 2020. To add insult to injury, Carmine has never beaten Andrew, 0-4 all-time, so this week doesn’t look like it will be a fun one for the team. In Week 7, the team continues to deal with key contributors on BYE like DJ Moore and Rachaad White, so almost all the odds are stacked against them. I still have faith in this team to hit their stride in the second half of the season.

teams.synopsis: Just like Brandon, Deniz is 2-4, on a losing streak, and averaging a mere 102 points per game.
teams.blurb: Just like Brandon, Deniz is 2-4, on a losing streak, and averaging a mere 102 points per game. Now, Deniz is an underdog against a team that has had their way with him since 2020, as Deniz is 1-5 against Quin all-time. Deniz has also failed to eclipse 100 points in back-to-back weeks, something that will likely need to change for his season to turn around. The team gets Amon-Ra St. Brown back from BYE and potential Josh Jacobs back from “suspension” in Week 7, so better days are likely ahead. However, I begin to second guess if that’s actually true since Deniz is projected to have one of the hardest strengths of schedule from this week and on. It’ll be a tough fight against a challenging opponent, but I think this team may have what it takes to avoid going three games under .500.

teams.synopsis: We’re in the midst of The Minutemen’s worst season to date.
teams.blurb: We’re in the midst of The Minutemen’s worst season to date. The team started 2-0 with 118.5 points per game, but since then they have gone 0-4 with 93.9 points per game, very uncharacteristic for one of the more successful managers in league history. To add to the misery, the team lost their starting QB for the rest of 2026 due to blood clots, forcing Brandon to make a trade for a new starting QB - Bryce Young. Unfortunately for Brandon, this cost him his best WR, Jalen Coker whom is averaging 17 points per game. I wasn’t a fan of the trade, but we’ll see how it plays out. Funny enough, Brandon matches up with Max in Week 7 so we’ll see the trade results unfold in real time. I think Bryce Young could finish as a top 10 QB this season, but the real X-factor in the deal has to be Dallas Goedert. This is now the second TE Brandon has traded for this season, the first being Harold Fannin Jr., but the team has only scored more than 10 points from the TE position two out six weeks so far in 2026, could Dallas Goedert flip the script?

matchup_of_the_week.blurb: Like last week’s Matchup of the Week, this week’s is between our top two ranked teams heading into Week 7. Hopefully unlike last week’s prime time game this one is actually high scoring and decides who takes the throne in Week 8. Aidan leads this matchup 4-1 all-time, but this time it’s Ben who is projected to get the win, according to ESPN analytics. The absence of Bhayshul Tuten and Mike Evans for Aidan will hurt, but I think he has enough depth to keep this one competitive, while Ben is without Kyle Monangai once again and Lamar Jackson’s availability is in question for a third week in a row. Here’s to hoping this matchup is a better viewing experience then last week’s.
